newsitem.title: MONTSERRAT: Rice row threatens volcano-troubled Montserrat.
newsitem.headline: Rice row threatens volcano-troubled Montserrat.

text.p: A row with the powerful European Union over rice export quotas threatens to do what the troublesome volcano on this tiny British colony has not been able to do, Montserrat's governor said -- shutter the rice mill.

The result of a David-and-Goliath battle between the tiny islands of the Caribbean and the EU will have a dramatic impact on the faltering economy of Montserrat, Gov. Frank Savage told Reuters this week.
"The volcano has not been able to close down the rice mill. The European Union might," Savage said.
The EU reduced imports of Caribbean rice as a result of complaints by Italian, Greek, French and Spanish farmers who said imports were distorting prices in the European market, Savage said.
Montserrat was told it could export just 4,650 metric tons of polished rice to Europe for the first four months of the year. Previously it sent all the mill could produce, up to 4,500 tons a month.

The mill, a critical facet of the colony's stumbling economy, sits at the foot of the island's rumbling volcano and has been kept operating despite the evacuation of surrounding Plymouth, the capital. It supports about 100 jobs at the factory and port.
The decrease promised to devastate the Caribbean rice industry, long protected by European quotas, Savage said.

The loss of the mill, a beacon to Montserratians plagued for 19 months by the Soufriere Hills volcano, would be a devastating blow to the economy, officials said. Unemployment has risen from 5 percent to 50 percent since the volcano became active in July 1995.

Savage said the port at Plymouth was dependent on rice shipments and without the mill, Montserrat would likely default on loans used to rebuild the harbour in 1989 after it was demolished by Hurricane Hugo.
Savage and Chief Minister Bertrand Osborne lobbied European Union officials on the issue in Brussels two weeks ago. A decision on future quotas was expected soon, Savage said.
